case_name: Rajinder Singh Gandhi vs Kunal Arora
facts_of_case: Complainant filed a complaint case u/s 138 NI Act titled as 'Kunal Arora V. Rajinder Singh Gandhi.' The revisionist has prayed to set-aside the orders passed by the trial court and to stay the trial.

legal_principles.principle: An interlocutory order is an order that does not decide the rights of the parties but only one aspect of the suit or trial.
legal_principles.held: It has been used in various statutes including the Code of Civil Procedure, Letters Patent of the High Courts and other like statutes. In Webster's New World Dictionary 'interlocutory' has been defined as an order other than final decision.
cited_cases: Amar Nath & Ors. V. State of Haryana & Anr., (1977) 4 SCC 137

legal_principles.principle: An order which does not determine the rights of the parties but only one aspect of the suit or the trial is an interlocutory order.
